issues.legal_issue: An eviction order founded principally on the landlord’s bona fide personal requirement remains an order on that ground when demolition and reconstruction are also mentioned, so the statutory duty to provide the tenants with accommodation in the new building does not apply.
material_facts: The landlord sought possession to locate a gold and silver ornaments factory on the premises after demolishing and reconstructing the building.
The lower courts found the landlord’s personal requirement bona fide and ordered eviction under both the personal-requirement ground and the reconstruction-related ground.
The tenants argued that the reconstruction-related ground made the statutory obligation to provide accommodation in the new building applicable.
issues.conclusion: The eviction order was in substance based on the landlord’s bona fide personal requirement; the additional reference to the reconstruction-related ground did not make it an order solely on that ground, and the statutory duty to provide accommodation in the new building did not apply.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 12(1)(f) and 12(1)(h) of the Madhya Pradesh Accommodation Control Act, 1961, the substance and principal basis of the eviction order determine which ground it rests on. Section 18 was not attracted because the order was substantially based on section 12(1)(f). Applying Ramnilal P. Mehta v. Indradaman Amritlal Sheth, AIR 1964 SC 1676, the Court held that a bona fide requirement for the landlord’s occupation remains such a ground whether occupation is to be without alterations or after necessary alterations; the corresponding Bombay provision was section 13(1)(g).

predicates.tenant_eviction_appeal: The tenants challenged an order evicting them from the premises.
predicates.bona_fide_personal_need_primary_ground: The courts found that the landlord principally required the premises bona fide for the landlord’s own proposed use.
predicates.reconstruction_ground_also_cited: The eviction order also referred to a ground involving demolition, reconstruction, or other building work.
predicates.statutory_rehousing_duty_not_triggered: The landlord is not required by the statutory rehousing duty to provide the evicted tenants with accommodation in the replacement building.

issues.definition: When tenants appeal an eviction order principally founded on the landlord’s bona fide personal need, an additional reference to a reconstruction ground does not trigger the statutory rehousing duty.

issues.legal_issue: An alleged alternative premises that is unsuitable for the landlord’s proposed business does not defeat a finding that the landlord bona fide requires the tenanted premises.
material_facts: The tenants asserted that the landlord had alternative accommodation for the proposed factory.
The lower courts found that the alternative premises was a farmhouse used to house farm servants, was remote from town, and was in a secluded location near a burial ground.
The lower courts found that the alternative premises was unsuitable for safely operating the proposed ornaments factory, and the Supreme Court agreed with that assessment.
issues.conclusion: The alleged alternative accommodation was unsuitable for the proposed factory, and the finding that the landlord’s requirement was bona fide was upheld.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied the bona fide personal-requirement ground in section 12(1)(f) of the Madhya Pradesh Accommodation Control Act, 1961, and upheld the lower courts’ factual assessment that the alleged alternative premises was unsuitable. No earlier case was relied on for this assessment.

predicates.tenant_eviction_appeal: The tenants challenged an order evicting them from the premises.
predicates.alternative_premises_unsuitable_for_prop: The alternative premises alleged by the tenants was unsuitable for the landlord’s proposed business use.
predicates.lower_courts_found_bona_fide_need: The lower courts found that the landlord bona fide required the premises for the proposed use.

issues.definition: In an appeal from an eviction order, an unsuitable alleged alternative premises supports sustaining the lower courts’ finding of bona fide need.
